passage: Note from Kalyani, school counsellor. Arnab, Class 6, asked to speak to me on Wednesday. He looked at his shoes and said an adult at his tuition centre had told him to keep an "arrangement" secret and to come to the back room alone. He said, "I'm supposed to do what elders tell me, but my tummy felt wrong." He told the adult no, walked out to the front desk, and later came to me. I said he was right to listen to that feeling and right to tell. What I did: I listened calmly, thanked him, told him none of it was his fault, kept him with me, and informed his parents and the school's child-protection lead the same day.

qa.q: Where was Arnab told to come alone?
qa.a: He was told to come alone to the back room.

qa.q: What was Arnab feeling when his tummy felt wrong, and what pulled him the other way?
qa.a: He was torn between obeying elders and a wrong feeling in his tummy that told him something was not okay.

qa.q: What did Arnab do that kept him safe?
qa.a: He said no, walked out to the front desk, and told a trusted adult, the counsellor.

qa.q: How might Arnab's parents feel when they learn what happened?
qa.a: They are likely worried, but also grateful he told and proud he listened to that feeling, and they will want him to know it is not his fault. 🤍

grounding: Shows a child told by an adult to keep a secret and come alone, feeling torn about obeying, who says no, leaves and tells a trusted adult.

passage:
Monday: The school-van uncle dropped Rajni and Dilnaz at the corner, far from the school gate, so he could go for tea. "Don't tell your parents," he said. "It's our secret. Children must obey elders." Rajni nodded, but her stomach stayed knotted all day.
Wednesday: He stopped near the school lane and told Rajni to stay alone in the van while he went into a shop. "And not a word to anyone." Rajni's heart hammered. Obey, said one voice. This feels wrong, said another. She grabbed her bag, said "No," climbed out with Dilnaz and walked straight to the school gate. She told the class teacher everything. The teacher thanked her, phoned both mothers at once, and the principal stopped that van before home time.
Friday: A new van driver waved them in. Mummy squeezed Rajni's hand. "You chose safety. That was exactly right."

qa.q: Where did the van uncle drop Rajni and Dilnaz on Monday?
qa.a: At the corner, far from the school gate.

qa.q: What was Rajni feeling when told to stay alone in the van?
qa.a: Torn and frightened; one voice said obey, another said it felt wrong, and her heart hammered.

qa.q: What did Rajni do, and what did the adults do the same day?
qa.a: She said no, left the van with Dilnaz and told the class teacher, who phoned both mothers; the principal stopped the van before home time.

qa.q: How did Mummy see Rajni's choice?
qa.a: As exactly right, because Rajni chose safety over obeying the driver.

grounding: A girl told by an adult to keep a secret and do something that feels wrong is torn, but says no, leaves and tells a trusted adult.

passage: Shreya, you asked if you must always obey grown-ups? Let your Hemant Chacha tell you something. When I was a boy, a landlord's man stopped me on the canal road. He gave me a tied cloth bundle and said, "Take this to the shed behind the mill. Tell nobody, not even your mother. Good boys obey elders." My legs went shaky. We were taught never to argue with elders, but my stomach said something was wrong. So I put the bundle down on the road, said "No," and ran all the way home. I told my mother. She didn't scold. That same evening she took me to the sarpanch, who called the police. So, Shreya: if a grown-up wants a secret that feels wrong, say no, walk away and tell us.

qa.q: Where was young Hemant told to take the bundle?
qa.a: To the shed behind the mill.

qa.q: What did young Hemant feel when the man gave him the bundle?
qa.a: Torn and scared; his legs went shaky because he was taught to obey elders but felt something was wrong.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Chacha's story?
qa.a: Putting the bundle down, saying no, running home and telling his mother.

qa.q: How did Hemant's mother respond when he told her?
qa.a: She did not scold; she took him to the sarpanch that same evening, and the sarpanch called the police.

grounding: An uncle recalls being told by an adult to keep a secret that felt wrong, and how saying no and telling his mother kept him safe.
